subject: Intermittent edge microburst — streaming latency advisory and mitigation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Delgado <rachel.delgado@atlaai.com>, AtlaAI Support <support@atlaai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent edge microburst — streaming latency advisory and mitigation

Hi Rachel / AtlaAI team,

We observed a short-lived edge capacity microburst this morning (09:05–09:20 PDT) that increased tail latency on streaming/chat endpoints for a subset of requests routed through our SFO edge. You may have seen delayed token delivery or brief pauses in streaming responses during that window.

What happened: our telemetry shows a transient spike in concurrent prefix cache misses combined with an autoscaler pod churn on a small edge pool. The combination caused queuing at the edge layer and delayed downstream token emission for ~1–2% of streaming sessions.

What we did immediately:
- Isolated the affected edge pool and drained it for a fast reboot.
- Temporarily scaled a warm spillover pool (SFO->SEA) to absorb traffic.
- Enabled short-duration prefetch for cached prefixes to reduce miss penalties.
- Deployed a graceful fallback in-routing to compatible model variants for connections that exceeded token-latency thresholds.

Short-term mitigations you can apply (no code change required in most cases):
- If you set a very aggressive client-side read timeout, consider increasing it by 300–500ms during peak windows.
- Accept and handle chunked partial outputs: treat early partial frames as deliverable responses rather than waiting for stream completion.
- If you use an internal concurrency knob, reduce your per-connection parallelism by 10–20% until we confirm long-term fixes.

We’ve attached the edge logs and a condensed timeline for your review. Apologies for the friction — we realize streaming UX is critical and are treating this with priority.

If you can share any session IDs or examples of affected requests (i.e., request id or timestamp), that’ll help correlate.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: edge-hotspot-logs-20250829.txt (text/plain), streaming-timelines-aug29.csv (text/csv)

Subject: Re: Intermittent edge microburst — streaming latency advisory and mitigation

Hi Rachel — thanks for the example request id, that was helpful. Quick answers and next steps:

Scope: The root cause was an autoscaler race on a small SFO edge pool that amplified a normal workload burst; we’ve found correlated but lower-severity cache-miss spikes in SEA and ORD during the same minute due to global propagation of short-prefetch metadata. Impact profile was heaviest in SFO; SEA/ORD saw sub-percent elevated latency but no resets reported.

Client tuning guidance (temporary, revert after we confirm long-term fixes):
- Read timeouts: increase by +400ms for interactive endpoints during high traffic windows (example: 2.5s -> 2.9s).
- Reconnect/backoff: enable exponential backoff with jitter for reconnect retries (initial delay 200ms, max 5s).
- Partial-frame acceptance: update client to render/stream partial frames as they arrive to avoid perceived stalls.

Server-side mitigations we’ve already queued:
- Autoscaler debounce change to reduce rapid pod churn (next deploy scheduled 2025-08-30 02:00 UTC).
- Edge prefetch tuning and increased warm pool sizing for SFO (rolling deploy started 09:40 PDT).
- A postmortem with telemetry is in progress; I’ve linked a work item in our incident tracker.

Compensation: we’re opening a case with Billing to apply a one-time service credit for impacted calls across your account for the 09:05–09:20 window. I’ll follow up with a precise credit amount tomorrow.

If you want a brief 20‑minute call this afternoon I can bring Marcus (runtime lead) and Priya (ops) to walk through telemetry and answer technical questions.

Sean
